consumption.basis: Australian ADR81/02 laboratory result for the original 2023 Extended: 149 Wh/km, reported by AAA from the Green Vehicle Guide. This is separate from AAA’s observed 18.0 kWh/100km. Do not relabel it WLTP; the source does not clearly define the energy boundary.

Australian ADR81/02 laboratory result: 148 Wh/km as reported by AAA for its 2025 Essential; separate from the 17.1 kWh/100km observed road test. Energy boundary is unspecified in the extracted report. This report has conflicting AC-capacity information, so its 11 kW AC statement is not treated as confirmed onboard capability.

safety.applicability: Related original-body 2022 five-star ANCAP result exists. Current ANCAP page broadly says all Australian variants, but the technical applicability table names Standard Range / Extended Range rather than the later Essential name. Exact Essential extension is not separately confirmed here; this is an applicability question, not an absence of safety evidence.

acCharging.basis: AC charging is supported: manufacturer Mode3 230–240 V / 15 A supply (about 3.6 kW supply power), with a claimed 6.5-hour charge; 9.5 hours at 10 A. A definitive onboard peak kW is not stated. Use the published charging time rather than confusing supply rating with vehicle limit.

dcCharging.basis: CHAdeMO DC fast charging is supported: manufacturer claims 38 minutes to 80%. Its Australian brochure does not state a vehicle peak kW, so a 50 kW external charger is not substituted as the onboard limit.
